name: Exelixis, Inc.
reason: Earnings rest almost entirely on cabozantinib, whose US patent exclusivity ends around 2030-31, so the 38.5% EBIT margin and EPS at 1.0x 10y peak face a drug patent cliff inside the forecast window.

name: ExlService Holdings, Inc.
reason: Excellent record (EPS up >=7% in 9/10 years, 0.16x net debt/EBITDA) but labour-based BPO/analytics revenue faces credible AI disintermediation within 5 years, and margin is at a 10y high of 15.1%.

name: Extra Space Storage Inc.
reason: Self-storage REIT with 6.35x net debt/EBITDA, FFO flat since 2022 (8.38 to 8.21) and consensus growth of 1.5-6%, so no plausible route to 7%/yr and growth came via share issuance (shares +5.3%/yr).

name: Extreme Networks, Inc.
reason: Sub-scale networking hardware vendor with a 1.9% 10y average EBIT margin and negative 10y average ROIC (-5.1%); no moat versus Cisco/HPE and adjusted EPS far above GAAP (152.8% gap).

name: EZCORP, Inc.
reason: Second-tier pawn lender with 2.4% 10y average ROIC, shares up 4.4%/yr, and EPS and margin both at 10y highs helped by record gold prices; a cheap but ordinary business.

name: FirstCash Holdings, Inc.
reason: Pawn leader with a long record, but growth is largely acquired (acq/FCF 0.71, shares +4.6%/yr, AFF lease-to-own deal), earnings currently boosted by record gold prices (EPS 1.0x 10y peak, margin 91st percentile), and Mexico/CFPB regulatory exposure.

name: Four Corners Property Trust, Inc.
reason: Net-lease restaurant REIT with FFO/share growth of only 1.1%/yr over 10 years (0/10 years >=7%) while shares grew 32%/yr; the 8.7% FCF yield is recurring rent but there is no route to 7% per-share growth.

name: Freeport-McMoRan, Inc.
reason: Copper/gold miner whose earnings are set by commodity prices (EPS swung from 0.02 to 3.13 within two years), plus Grasberg operational and Indonesia regulatory risk.

name: FirstEnergy Corp.
reason: Regulated utility with EPS flat for a decade (-0.6% 10y CAGR), 6.1x net debt/EBITDA, negative FCF (-11.4% yield) and a history of Ohio HB6 bribery-scandal regulatory risk.

name: Fair Isaac Corporation
reason: Superb economics (EPS up >=7% in 10/10 years, 47% EBIT margin, 30% ROIC) but recent growth was mostly mortgage-score price increases, and FHFA/regulator moves on lender score choice, bureau direct licensing and pricing scrutiny are a credible regulatory threat within 5 years; net debt/EBITDA is 3.1x from buybacks.

name: Figure Technology Solutions, Inc.
reason: Recently IPO'd HELOC originator/securitizer and blockchain/crypto marketplace with only three years of history; earnings depend on credit, rates and capital-markets activity, and LTM CFO is -$6.6bn.

name: Flowserve Corporation
reason: Cyclical pump/valve maker with EPS 1.0x 10y peak and margin in the 91st percentile after a sharp run-up, yet 10y EPS CAGR is only 1.7% and revenue CAGR 0.3%; an ordinary industrial.

name: First Industrial Realty Trust, Inc.
reason: Well-run industrial REIT (FFO up 8.8%/yr) but the growth came from a rent mark-to-market tailwind that is fading (consensus LTG 3%), margin is at a 10y high, net debt/EBITDA is 5.1x, and it has no clear specialness against larger peers.

name: Freshworks, Inc.
reason: SMB help-desk/ITSM SaaS that only reached GAAP profitability in 2025 (EBIT margin 1.6%), faces direct AI-agent disintermediation in customer service, and the 7.6% FCF yield is flattered by heavy stock compensation.

name: Frontdoor, Inc.
reason: Home-warranty leader with 18% ROIC and 1.2x leverage, but member counts fell for years and the 2023-25 EPS rebound (to 1.0x peak) came from price rises and claims-cost relief after the 2022 collapse (-33%); FCF is recurring but the margin path is hard to forecast.

name: Fortive Corp.
reason: Serial acquirer (acq/FCF 1.12) that just spun off Precision Technologies (Ralliant) in 2025, so the remaining portfolio has no clean history; 10y EPS CAGR is 6.1% with consensus LTG of 1.5%.

name: Six Flags Entertainment Corporation
reason: Post-merger regional theme-park operator with losses (2025 EPS -15.87), 7.0x net debt/EBITDA and acquisition-driven size (acq/FCF 7.9); the 25% NTM FCF yield is a forecast, not demonstrated (LTM FCF negative).

name: Greif Inc
reason: Cyclical industrial packaging with EPS at 0.25x 10y peak and margin in the 9th percentile, acquisition-driven (acq/FCF 1.33); the 8.7% NTM FCF yield follows the containerboard divestiture and LTM FCF was negative.

name: Genesis Energy, L.P.
reason: Leveraged midstream MLP (5.9x net debt/EBITDA) with losses in 5 of the last 8 years and soda-ash/commodity exposure; the 14.8% FCF yield is a forecast after asset sales, not recurring proven FCF.

name: GEO Group Inc
reason: Private prisons/detention dependent on a few government customers (ICE) and federal policy, so it faces binary political risk; EPS fell -4.2%/yr over 10y, leverage is 3.8x, and LTM FCF was negative despite the 7.4% NTM yield.
